summary: Properties of determiners on finite universes, after Barwise and Cooper. The logical determiners live on their first argument; their monotonicity and persistence profiles; results C1, C4, C5, C7, C9 and C10 of the paper's Appendix C; and separating examples, among them 'only' read as a determiner, which is not conservative.

sources.citation: Barwise, J. & Cooper, R. (1981). Generalized quantifiers and natural language. Linguistics and Philosophy 4(2): 159-219.

theorems.name: only_not_conservative
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 1 (ours): "only" does not live on its first argument. Only men run is false (3 runs), only men are men who run is true.

theorems.name: some_not_all_separates
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 3 (p. 211): "some but not all" is persistent but neither mon-up nor symmetric. So C7 needs its symmetry premise.

theorems.name: every_not_intersective
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 4 (instance of C6, p. 211): "every" is positive strong and fails the intersection condition, hence (C5) is not symmetric.

theorems.name: some_meets_premises
theorems.source_claim: Non-vacuity of T4, T6: "some" meets every premise of C5 and C7, and the conclusions are obtained through those theorems.

theorems.name: C6_premises_satisfiable
theorems.source_claim: Non-vacuity of T5: the premises of C6 are jointly satisfiable (by the trivial determiner), and by T5 only trivially.

theorems.name: C10_instance
theorems.source_claim: Non-vacuity of T8: Q = more than half the men; run is in Q, {0,1} is in the dual of Q, and C10 yields a common element.

theorems.name: duals_on_model
theorems.source_claim: Duals, checked on all 32 x 32 pairs of subsets of E5. p. 197: the dual of "some man" is "every man"; pp. 198-199: the dual of "more than half" is "at least half".

theorems.name: self_dual_odd
theorems.source_claim: p. 197: on a set of odd cardinality "more than half" is self-dual (man has 3 elements); on one of even cardinality it is not (ours).

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.
Determiners are total here. C6 concerns proper strong determiners, which needs partial determiners; the file proves the claim established inside the proof of C6 and says so.
Counting determiners count members only when the universe has no repetition; the file states and proves this.
